subject: shinyAce - prevent/override default editor behaviour when Tab key is down

messages.author: a417fa537bba98f2
messages.subject: shinyAce - prevent/override default editor behaviour when Tab key is down
parts:
Dear All,

I am trying to override or at least prevent the line indenting triggered by the Tab key in the aceEditor and use said key for something else (in this case navigating the inputs).

Within my project users are unlikely to write code in the editor (making indenting less crucial), I would like to see if allowing them to navigate all inputs using Tab & Shift+Tab could be a plus for them.

So far I haven't been able to override the indenting behaviour though I can achieve something similar with other keys. It doesn't work when I change the keycode 176 to 9. A small example here:

UI

library(shiny)
library(shinyAce)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
    mainPanel(
      includeScript("moveFocusOnTab.js"),
      h5(tags$strong("Tags")),
      aceEditor("elementTags", value="", mode="text", theme="ambient", readOnly = FALSE,
                height = "60px", fontSize = 12, wordWrap = TRUE),
      h5(tags$strong("Description")),
      aceEditor("elementDescription", value="", mode="text", theme="ambient", readOnly = FALSE,
                height = "60px", fontSize = 12, wordWrap = TRUE)
    )
))


JS

jQuery(document).ready(function(){
  jQuery("#elementTags").keydown(function (e) {   
  if (e.which == 176) {
    e.preventDefault();
// the alert is to make sure the script is running but we don't want anything showing in the editor
    alert('Key pressed!');
  }
});
})

I assume that once I can prevent the default indenting, moving focus to an other input should be easy.

Thanks in advance for reading this and for any hint.

Best regards,

Bastien

messages.subject: Re: shinyAce - prevent/override default editor behaviour when Tab key is down
parts:
Update:

using the 'hotkeys' parameter in aceEditor() I am able to 'catch' the tab keydown event (indenting doesn't occur anymore):

hotkeys = list (nextInputKey = list(win="Tab", mac="Tab"))

Now I am looking for a way to trigger blur() and focus() on the UI side with input.nextInputKey.

I should be able to do something with the shinyjs library but I am still wondering if there is a more 'shinywise' way to do that that anyone knows of?

Best,
Bastien

messages.author: a417fa537bba98f2
messages.subject: Re: shinyAce - prevent/override default editor behaviour when Tab key is down
parts:
Solved via javascript.

I changed moveFocusOnTab.js to:

jQuery(document).ready(function(){
  var elementTags = ace.edit("elementTags");
elementTags.commands.bindKey("Tab",null);
elementTags.commands.bindKey("Shift+Tab",null);
    }
);

I had seen that editor.commands.bindKey() was the obvious solution on many threads but I always failed to capture the editor object as I didn't know of ace.edit().

Bastien
